newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Edison to buy out Australia plant - report.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Edison to buy out Australia plant - report.

text.p: Edison Mission Energy, a unit of U.S. utility Edison International, is negotiating to move to full ownership of the big Loy Yang B power station in Australia's Victoria state, a newspaper reported on Tuesday.

The Age newspaper report, quoting unnamed sources, said Edison wanted to buy the Victoria government's remaining 49 percent equity in the coal-fired plant in a deal that would be worth over A$1 billion.
A spokesman for Victoria Treasurer Alan Stockdale declined to comment on the report.
The plant near Melbourne has two 500 megawatt generators.
Edison moved to 51 percent of Loy Yang B in late 1992. Since then Stockdale has said he would like to sell the government's remaining stake, held through its utility PowerNet Victoria.
The Victoria government has so far sold over A$12 billion worth of electricity assets, including the 1,600 megawatt Hazelwood coal-fired station last August.
A spokesman for Edison was not immediately available.

The government is also putting its Loy Yang A power station on the block. The Loy Yang A sale, which includes a coal mine, is expected to fetch up to A$5 billion for the state government, according to media reports. -- Melbourne bureau 61-3 9286-1421
